materials.name: Polylactic Acid (PLA)
materials.biobased_feedstock: Typically fermented plant starch / sugars (corn, sugarcane, cassava)

general_characteristics.typical_applications: Rigid packaging, thermoformed cups, cold beverage cups, 3D printing filaments, agricultural films

industrial_compost.label: Evidence supports biodegradation under the specified conditions
industrial_compost.conditions: Thermophilic composting (temperature ≥ 58 °C, relative humidity > 60%, active microbial consortium)
industrial_compost.summary: Neat PLA undergoes abiotic hydrolytic chain cleavage above its glass transition temperature (~58 °C), reducing molecular weight until thermophilic microorganisms assimilate lactic acid monomers and oligomers.
references: Narancic et al., Environ. Sci. Technol. 2018
industrial_compost.limitations: Requires thermophilic industrial facilities. Crystallinity and article wall thickness significantly slow degradation. Does not disintegrate in ambient home compost or open landfill.

home_compost.label: Evidence indicates low biodegradation under the specified conditions
home_compost.summary: Temperatures in standard home compost bins remain well below PLA's glass transition temperature (~58 °C). Hydrolysis occurs at an extremely slow rate; macroscopic items persist with negligible mass loss over standard 12-month periods.
home_compost.limitations: Only specialized chemically modified low-molecular-weight or heavily plasticized oligomeric formulations pass home composting standards; neat high-MW PLA does not.

soil.label: Evidence indicates low biodegradation under the specified conditions
soil.conditions: Natural soil (ambient temperate climate 15 - 25 °C, natural pH 6-8)
soil.summary: Soil temperatures are insufficient to trigger thermal-hydrolytic scission. Multi-year burial studies document intact fragments with <5% degradation over 1-2 years.
soil.limitations: Cannot be used as biodegradable mulch without blending with fast-degrading polyesters (PBAT, starch).

freshwater.label: Evidence indicates low biodegradation under the specified conditions
freshwater.summary: Aqueous hydrolysis at ambient temperature is negligible; absence of thermophilic microbial communities leads to prolonged aquatic persistence.
freshwater.limitations: Items will persist in rivers, lakes, and freshwater reservoirs.

marine.label: Evidence indicates low biodegradation under the specified conditions
marine.conditions: Marine pelagic and benthic seawater (10 - 20 °C, high salinity, low nutrient levels)
marine.summary: Pelagic exposure tests demonstrate virtually zero mass loss (<1-2% after 1 year) due to low oceanic temperatures and lack of PLA-depolymerase enzymes in marine microbial consortia.
marine.limitations: Presents persistent macro- and micro-plastic pollution risk in marine habitats identical to non-degradable polymers.

materials.disintegration_vs_biodegradation_notes: Physical fragmentation into particles <2mm (disintegration) must not be confused with enzymatic mineralization to CO2, H2O, and biomass. Unmineralized fragments persist as microplastics if ambient conditions prevent microbial uptake.
materials.recyclability_notes: Recyclable in dedicated PLA closed-loop mechanical systems, but contaminates conventional PET recycling streams (Code 1) at concentrations as low as 0.1% due to similar density and thermal degradation during PET remelting.
materials.ecotoxicity_notes: Pure PLA degrades to lactic acid, which enters the Krebs cycle. However, formulated PLA may contain catalyst residues (e.g., organotin like tin(II) octoate) and optical additives requiring chemical screening.

materials.name: Polyhydroxyalkanoates (PHA: PHB / PHBV)
materials.biobased_feedstock: Intracellular microbial bacterial synthesis via bacterial fermentation of sugars, vegetable oils, or waste volatile fatty acids

general_characteristics.typical_applications: Films, injection molded goods, single-use cutlery, marine gear, medical sutures

industrial_compost.label: Evidence supports biodegradation under the specified conditions
industrial_compost.summary: Rapid microbial enzymatic depolymerization by extracellular PHA depolymerases; typically reaches >90% CO2 evolution well within the 180-day window.
industrial_compost.limitations: High crystallinity of homopolymer PHB may retard degradation if processing parameters result in large spherulites.

home_compost.label: Evidence supports biodegradation under the specified conditions
home_compost.summary: Ubiquitous mesophilic bacteria and fungi express extracellular PHA depolymerases that hydrolyze PHA into water-soluble hydroxy acids, which are readily mineralized.
home_compost.limitations: Wall thickness must be controlled; articles over 1-2 mm require extended disintegration time.

soil.label: Evidence supports biodegradation under the specified conditions
soil.summary: Soil microorganisms readily colonize PHA surfaces, achieving high levels of mineralization without synthetic chemical residues.
soil.limitations: Moisture, soil microbial biomass, and temperature influence rate; cold arctic or arid soils degrade significantly slower.

freshwater.label: Evidence supports biodegradation under the specified conditions
freshwater.summary: Aquatic bacteria mineralize PHA films and particles, achieving respirometric criteria within standard testing timeframes.
freshwater.limitations: Rate depends on water eutrophication status and temperature.

marine.label: Evidence supports biodegradation under the specified conditions
marine.summary: PHA is one of the few polymer classes with verifiable enzymatic depolymerization by marine biofilm communities (e.g., Pseudoalteromonas and marine fungi).
marine.limitations: Degradation in deep, near-freezing ocean waters (>1000m, ~2 °C) is significantly slower. Marine certification does not endorse open marine littering.

materials.disintegration_vs_biodegradation_notes: PHA degrades via surface enzymatic erosion rather than bulk abiotic hydrolysis. Surface erosion leads directly to microbial assimilation without persistent intermediate fragments.
materials.recyclability_notes: Low thermal stability makes mechanical recycling via repeated re-extrusion challenging without significant chain scission and degradation.
materials.ecotoxicity_notes: Microbial metabolite 3-hydroxybutyrate is inherently biocompatible (found in human blood as a ketone body). Plant and aquatic ecotoxicity tests consistently show non-toxic behavior.

materials.name: Polybutylene Adipate Terephthalate (PBAT)
materials.biobased_feedstock: Typically petrochemical fossil-derived (adipic acid, 1,4-butanediol, terephthalic acid), though bio-based BDO/adipic acid routes exist

general_characteristics.typical_applications: Flexible film packaging, agricultural mulch film, compostable garbage bags (often blended with PLA or starch)

industrial_compost.label: Evidence supports biodegradation under the specified conditions
industrial_compost.summary: Aliphatic-aromatic ester bonds are cleaved by microbial esterases and abiotic hydrolysis at elevated compost temperatures, achieving >90% conversion within 180 days.
industrial_compost.limitations: Compost facility residence times below 60 days may result in visible flexible film fragments.

home_compost.label: Limited or condition-specific evidence
home_compost.summary: Thin PBAT films (<20-30 μm) can pass home composting disintegration and biodegradation standards, but thicker sections degrade sluggishly due to the aromatic terephthalate segments.
home_compost.limitations: Strictly thickness-dependent; thick films or injection molded PBAT do not pass home composting criteria.

soil.label: Evidence supports biodegradation under the specified conditions
soil.summary: Qualified under EN 17033 for agricultural mulch films at prescribed gauges (typically ≤25 μm), mineralized by soil fungi and bacteria over 1-2 years.
soil.limitations: Accumulation risk if applied annually in heavy clay or cold climates without proper soil turnover.

freshwater.label: Limited or condition-specific evidence
freshwater.summary: Shows moderate, slow biodegradation in freshwater; typically slower than aliphatic polyesters.
freshwater.limitations: Does not achieve rapid aquatic dissolution or mineralization.

marine.label: Evidence indicates low biodegradation under the specified conditions
marine.summary: PBAT shows very slow mass loss in open seawater. While higher than polyolefins, it does not fulfill marine biodegradability specifications within practical timeframes.
marine.limitations: Persistent hazard if littered in marine waters.

materials.disintegration_vs_biodegradation_notes: PBAT provides ductility to PLA/starch blends. If degradation conditions are incomplete, flexible micro-fragments containing aromatic terephthalate oligomers may linger.
materials.recyclability_notes: Incompatible with standard low-density polyethylene (LDPE) recycling streams; causes severe melt flow instability and black specks/smoke during polyolefin recycling.
materials.ecotoxicity_notes: Passing EN 17033 certification requires plant germination tests and soil earthworm ecotoxicity clearance.

materials.name: Polybutylene Succinate (PBS)
materials.biobased_feedstock: Partially biobased (bio-succinic acid and/or bio-1,4-butanediol) or synthetic fossil-derived

general_characteristics.typical_applications: Thermoformed packaging, agricultural mulch, coffee capsules, film blowing

industrial_compost.label: Evidence supports biodegradation under the specified conditions
industrial_compost.summary: Linear aliphatic polyester chain structure is susceptible to enzymatic esterase attack; achieves >90% biodegradation within 180 days under ISO 14855.
industrial_compost.limitations: Higher crystallinity than PBAT results in slightly slower initial disintegration kinetics.

home_compost.label: Limited or condition-specific evidence
home_compost.summary: PBS homopolymer exhibits slow degradation in home compost. Copolymers like PBSA (Polybutylene succinate-co-adipate) degrade significantly faster at ambient temperatures.
home_compost.limitations: Neat high-crystallinity PBS items often exceed home composting time thresholds unless formulated as copolymers.

soil.label: Limited or condition-specific evidence
soil.summary: Biodegrades over 12-24 months in soil depending heavily on film thickness, microbial activity, and copolymer ratio.
soil.limitations: Standard PBS thicker than 50 μm requires several seasons to achieve high mineralization.

freshwater.label: Limited or condition-specific evidence
freshwater.summary: Slow aquatic biodegradation observed; relies on specific esterase-producing aquatic bacteria.
freshwater.limitations: Prolonged residence time in oligotrophic water bodies.

marine.label: Evidence indicates low biodegradation under the specified conditions
marine.summary: In seawater without benthic anaerobic sediment, PBS exhibits very low degradation rates (<5-10% in 180 days).
marine.limitations: Cannot be considered marine biodegradable under open ocean conditions.

materials.disintegration_vs_biodegradation_notes: Spherulite crystallization can yield brittle macroscopic fragments before enzymatic cleavage is completed.
materials.recyclability_notes: Can be chemically or mechanically reprocessed in isolated streams; incompatible with polyolefin or PET recycling streams.
materials.ecotoxicity_notes: Succinic acid and 1,4-butanediol metabolites are readily metabolized with low demonstrated toxicity in standard plant assays.

materials.name: Thermoplastic Starch (TPS)
materials.biobased_feedstock: Corn, potato, cassava, or wheat starch plasticized with polyols (glycerol, sorbitol, water)

general_characteristics.typical_applications: Carrier bags, packaging foams, loose-fill, blends with PBAT or PLA

industrial_compost.label: Evidence supports biodegradation under the specified conditions
industrial_compost.summary: Readily depolymerized by amylase enzymes from diverse microbial populations; typically reaches >90% mineralization in under 4-8 weeks.
industrial_compost.limitations: Hydrophilic nature requires blending or protective barrier coatings for functional packaging.

home_compost.label: Evidence supports biodegradation under the specified conditions
home_compost.summary: Microbial amylolytic activity in ambient compost rapidly converts amylose and amylopectin into glucose and biomass within weeks to months.
home_compost.limitations: Co-formulated synthetic resins in commercial starch blends dictate the final home compostability.

soil.label: Evidence supports biodegradation under the specified conditions
soil.summary: Native soil fungi and bacteria rapidly metabolize starch; high mineralization rates confirmed in soil respirometry.
soil.limitations: None for pure starch, but commercial TPS is almost always blended with polyesters (PBAT) which determine the overall degradation timescale.

freshwater.label: Evidence supports biodegradation under the specified conditions
freshwater.summary: Water solubility and high bioavailability lead to rapid aerobic aqueous biodegradation.
freshwater.limitations: High biological oxygen demand (BOD) if discharged in large bulk quantities into stagnant waterways.

marine.label: Evidence supports biodegradation under the specified conditions
marine.summary: Marine microorganisms rapidly consume starch polysaccharides, leaving no persistent residue.
marine.limitations: TPS alone lacks water resistance; commercial blends with PBAT/PLA will retain the marine persistence profile of those hydrophobic components.

materials.disintegration_vs_biodegradation_notes: Starch dissolves/disperses rapidly in water, which must not be conflated with total mineralization, although microbial respiration follows rapidly.
materials.recyclability_notes: Severe contaminant in conventional polyolefin and PET mechanical recycling; causes foaming, charring, and caramelization at plastic extrusion temperatures.
materials.ecotoxicity_notes: Food-grade polysaccharide matrix with non-toxic glycerol plasticizers; passes all terrestrial and aquatic ecotoxicity benchmarks.

materials.name: Regenerated Cellulose / Cellophane
materials.biobased_feedstock: Wood pulp or cotton linters processed via viscose or lyocell / NMMO dissolution

general_characteristics.typical_applications: Clear film wraps, confectionery packaging, tape backing, breathable bags

industrial_compost.label: Evidence supports biodegradation under the specified conditions
industrial_compost.summary: Serves as the international standard reference material (positive control) for ISO 14855 and ASTM D6400; reaches >90% CO2 conversion in under 45 days.
industrial_compost.limitations: Requires uncoated or biopolymer-coated film; traditional PVDC or nitrocellulose coatings prevent compostability.

home_compost.label: Evidence supports biodegradation under the specified conditions
home_compost.summary: Cellulolytic enzymes produced by common composting fungi (Trichoderma, Aspergillus) hydrolyze beta-1,4-glucan bonds rapidly.
home_compost.limitations: Synthetic barrier coatings (e.g. PVDC) will remain as micro-coatings if present.

soil.label: Evidence supports biodegradation under the specified conditions
soil.summary: Rapidly mineralized by native soil cellulolytic bacteria and fungi within 6-12 weeks in humid soil.
soil.limitations: Dry arid soils slow microbial colonization.

freshwater.label: Evidence supports biodegradation under the specified conditions
freshwater.summary: Degrades readily in natural freshwater environments containing active aquatic microflora.
freshwater.limitations: Uncoated films hydrate and soften quickly.

marine.label: Evidence supports biodegradation under the specified conditions
marine.summary: Substantial microbial mineralization documented in coastal and benthic marine environments, where cellulase-producing marine bacteria break down cellulose fibers.
marine.limitations: Waterproof synthetic barrier coatings will persist.

materials.disintegration_vs_biodegradation_notes: Uncoated cellulose fibers biodegrade directly without intermediate persistent synthetic particles.
materials.recyclability_notes: Can be repulped in paper recycling streams if compatible with de-inking / pulping systems; not recyclable in plastic streams.
materials.ecotoxicity_notes: Completely benign natural polysaccharide matrix; chemical coatings (lacquers) require independent ecotoxicological testing.

materials.name: Cellulose Acetate (CA)
materials.biobased_feedstock: Acetylated cellulose from wood pulp or cotton

general_characteristics.typical_applications: Cigarette filter tows, eyewear frames, transparent films, textiles

industrial_compost.label: Limited or condition-specific evidence
industrial_compost.summary: Biodegradation is strictly dependent on the Degree of Substitution (DS). Low DS (<2.1) shows moderate to good biodegradation under industrial composting, whereas higher DS (>2.5) exhibits high microbial resistance.
industrial_compost.limitations: Commercial cigarette filters and plastics typically have DS ~2.5 and contain plasticizers (triacetin), showing prolonged composting times.

home_compost.label: Evidence indicates low biodegradation under the specified conditions
home_compost.summary: Ambient temperatures provide insufficient enzymatic deacetylation rates for standard commercial CA grades.
home_compost.limitations: Neat commercial grades fail home compost standards.

soil.label: Evidence indicates low biodegradation under the specified conditions
soil.summary: Soil burial studies demonstrate that conventional cellulose acetate tows require 5 to 14 years to break down in open soil environments.
soil.limitations: Primary component of discarded cigarette butts, representing widespread global soil litter persistence.

freshwater.label: Evidence indicates low biodegradation under the specified conditions
freshwater.summary: Extremely slow deacetylation in natural water; persists for multiple years in freshwater habitats.
freshwater.limitations: High environmental persistence in rivers and lakes.

marine.label: Evidence indicates low biodegradation under the specified conditions
marine.summary: Exhibits long persistence in marine conditions; cigarette filters remain recognizable after years of marine immersion.
marine.limitations: Leaches toxic accumulated nicotine and heavy metals when discarded as smoked filters.

materials.disintegration_vs_biodegradation_notes: Filters fibrillate mechanically into microfibers that persist for years due to the acetyl substituent groups blocking cellulase access.
materials.recyclability_notes: Specialty thermoplastic processing; cannot be mixed into municipal plastic recycling streams.
materials.ecotoxicity_notes: Unused pure polymer has low toxicity, but secondary plasticizers (phthalates or triacetin) and user-contaminants dictate real-world ecotoxicity.

materials.name: Polyethylene (PE: LDPE / LLDPE / HDPE)
materials.biobased_feedstock: Typically petrochemical; bio-based ethylene produces chemically indistinguishable Bio-PE

general_characteristics.typical_applications: Shopping bags, milk jugs, squeeze bottles, agricultural mulch, geomembranes

industrial_compost.label: Evidence indicates low biodegradation under the specified conditions
industrial_compost.summary: Inert carbon-carbon single bond backbone with high molecular weight and hydrophobicity prevents microbial attack; zero measurable respirometric biodegradation.
industrial_compost.limitations: Severe contaminant in compost streams, leading to reject batches and microplastic contamination of agricultural compost.

home_compost.label: Evidence indicates low biodegradation under the specified conditions
home_compost.summary: Zero biological breakdown; remains completely unaltered in home compost heaps.

soil.label: Evidence indicates low biodegradation under the specified conditions
soil.summary: Requires decades to centuries for UV-induced photo-oxidation followed by negligible microbial erosion; accumulates as persistent micro- and nano-plastics.
soil.limitations: Major driver of microplastic buildup in agricultural soils from conventional mulch film fragments.

freshwater.label: Evidence indicates low biodegradation under the specified conditions
freshwater.summary: Hydrophobic non-polar surface resists bio-assimilation; persists and adsorbs organic contaminants.

marine.label: Evidence indicates low biodegradation under the specified conditions
marine.summary: Buoyant (density < 1.0 g/cm3), floats on sea surface, fragments slowly via solar UV into secondary microplastics over decades to centuries without biological mineralization.
marine.limitations: One of the most ubiquitous ocean plastic pollutants worldwide.

materials.disintegration_vs_biodegradation_notes: Under UV and mechanical wave action, PE fragments into microplastics. This is abiotic physical fragmentation, NOT biodegradation or mineralization.
materials.recyclability_notes: Excellent mechanical recyclability with mature global infrastructure (Resin Identification Codes 2 and 4).
materials.ecotoxicity_notes: Virgin polymer is biologically inert; risk arises from plasticizer/additive migration and adsorption of persistent organic pollutants (POPs) on microplastic surfaces.

materials.name: Polypropylene (PP)
materials.biobased_feedstock: Petrochemical fossil feedstock; emerging bio-propylene routes yield identical polymer

general_characteristics.typical_applications: Bottle caps, food containers, yogurt cups, automotive parts, woven bags

industrial_compost.label: Evidence indicates low biodegradation under the specified conditions
industrial_compost.summary: Extremely resistant aliphatic C-C backbone; no enzymatic degradation observed under composting conditions.

home_compost.label: Evidence indicates low biodegradation under the specified conditions
home_compost.summary: Complete persistence; no biological degradation occurs.

soil.label: Evidence indicates low biodegradation under the specified conditions
soil.summary: No verified biodegradation by soil microorganisms in the absence of severe thermal-photo-oxidative pre-treatment.

freshwater.label: Evidence indicates low biodegradation under the specified conditions
freshwater.summary: Persistent in water bodies; undergoes mechanical fragmentation without microbial digestion.

marine.label: Evidence indicates low biodegradation under the specified conditions
marine.summary: Floats on water; degrades abiotically via sunlight into microplastic fibers and beads without complete carbon mineralization.
marine.limitations: Persistent threat to seabirds, marine turtles, and marine filter feeders.

materials.disintegration_vs_biodegradation_notes: Photo-oxidation creates tertiary carbon radicals that lead to embrittlement and disintegration into microplastics, not enzymatic mineralization.
materials.recyclability_notes: Widely mechanically recycled (Resin Identification Code 5). High demand for clean rPP streams.
materials.ecotoxicity_notes: Virgin polymer is food-contact safe, but thermal stabilizers and UV absorbers may have environmental toxicity profiles.

materials.name: Polyethylene Terephthalate (PET)
materials.biobased_feedstock: Typically petrochemical; Bio-PET (e.g. 30% bio-based MEG) has identical chemical structure

general_characteristics.typical_applications: Beverage bottles, thermoformed clamshells, polyester fibers/textiles

industrial_compost.label: Evidence indicates low biodegradation under the specified conditions
industrial_compost.summary: High melting point, aromatic ring stability, and high crystallinity prevent significant enzymatic hydrolysis in composting facilities.
industrial_compost.limitations: Engineered bacterial PETases operate under laboratory bioreactor conditions, not commercial composting environments.

home_compost.label: Evidence indicates low biodegradation under the specified conditions
home_compost.summary: No degradation observed; bottles and fibers remain unaltered.

soil.label: Evidence indicates low biodegradation under the specified conditions
soil.summary: Estimated degradation half-life exceeds centuries in soil environments.

freshwater.label: Evidence indicates low biodegradation under the specified conditions
freshwater.summary: Non-buoyant (sinks); accumulates in sediment beds with virtually zero microbial assimilation.
freshwater.limitations: Sinks and smothers benthic sediment ecosystems.

marine.label: Evidence indicates low biodegradation under the specified conditions
marine.summary: Sinks to sea bottom due to density (1.38 g/cm3); cold deep-sea benthic environments preserve PET bottles for decades without degradation.

materials.disintegration_vs_biodegradation_notes: Textile PET sheds microfibers during laundering; these synthetic fibers do not biodegrade in municipal wastewater treatment plants or aquatic systems.
materials.recyclability_notes: Highest mechanical recycling volume globally (Resin Identification Code 1, rPET bottle-to-bottle). Contaminated by PLA or PVC.
materials.ecotoxicity_notes: Antimony trioxide catalyst residue is monitored for food-contact migration limits; overall polymer matrix is non-toxic.

materials.name: Polystyrene (PS / EPS)

general_characteristics.typical_applications: Protective packaging, foam food containers, disposable cutlery, petri dishes

industrial_compost.label: Evidence indicates low biodegradation under the specified conditions
industrial_compost.summary: Aromatic pendant groups and durable C-C backbones prevent biological mineralization.

home_compost.label: Evidence indicates low biodegradation under the specified conditions
home_compost.summary: Completely persistent in home compost bins.

soil.label: Evidence indicates low biodegradation under the specified conditions
soil.summary: While insect larvae (e.g. mealworms) can chew and pass EPS, carbon mineralization is minimal (<5-10%); the bulk passes as microplastic frass.

freshwater.label: Evidence indicates low biodegradation under the specified conditions
freshwater.summary: Floats and persists in rivers and lakes.

marine.label: Evidence indicates low biodegradation under the specified conditions
marine.summary: EPS foams fragment under wave impact into millions of buoyant spherical beads (microplastics) that persist across ocean gyres.
marine.limitations: Severe widespread ingestion hazard for marine organisms.

materials.disintegration_vs_biodegradation_notes: Mechanical fragmentation of EPS into beads gives an illusion of disappearance, but represents hazardous microplastic pollution.
materials.recyclability_notes: Very low economic recycling rates due to bulky transportation of expanded foam; poor circular infrastructure (Resin Identification Code 6).
materials.ecotoxicity_notes: Residual styrene monomer is classified as probably carcinogenic to humans (IARC Group 2A); flame retardants (e.g. HBCD) present persistent organic pollutant concerns in construction EPS.

materials.name: Polyvinyl Chloride (PVC)
materials.biobased_feedstock: Petrochemical ethylene + chlorine from rock salt electrolysis

general_characteristics.typical_applications: Pipes, medical tubing, cable insulation, blister packaging, faux leather

industrial_compost.label: Evidence indicates low biodegradation under the specified conditions
industrial_compost.summary: Chlorinated backbone prevents microbial colonization; emits toxic organochlorine compounds if incinerated.

home_compost.label: Evidence indicates low biodegradation under the specified conditions

soil.label: Evidence indicates low biodegradation under the specified conditions
soil.summary: Persists for centuries in soil. Plasticizer additives (e.g. phthalates) leach into soil groundwater while polymer matrix remains.

freshwater.label: Evidence indicates low biodegradation under the specified conditions

marine.label: Evidence indicates low biodegradation under the specified conditions
marine.summary: Sinks to ocean floor and persists for centuries without biological carbon mineralization.

materials.disintegration_vs_biodegradation_notes: PVC does not biodegrade. It undergoes dehydrochlorination under intense heat/UV, producing dark polyene sequences and toxic HCl.
materials.recyclability_notes: Major contaminant in PET and polyolefin recycling streams; 50 ppm PVC ruins PET recycling batches due to acid generation.
materials.ecotoxicity_notes: High ecotoxicity concern from ortho-phthalate plasticizers (endocrine disruptors) and heavy metal thermal stabilizers (organotin, lead, barium-zinc).

materials.name: Calcium Carbonate (CaCO3 Filler)
materials.biobased_feedstock: Mined natural mineral (calcite) or precipitated calcium carbonate

general_characteristics.typical_applications: Inorganic mineral filler in bioplastic bags, thermoformed trays, injection molding to reduce cost and increase stiffness

industrial_compost.label: Limited or condition-specific evidence
industrial_compost.conditions: Composting medium (slightly acidic to neutral pH)
industrial_compost.summary: Inorganic mineral: cannot undergo organic biological mineralization (no organic carbon to evolve CO2). Under composting conditions, it acts as an inert neutralizer; standard compost specifications (EN 13432) cap total inorganic filler/ash content to ensure finished compost quality.
industrial_compost.limitations: Does NOT biodegrade. High loadings (>10-20%) can breach compost volatile solids limits (>50% volatile solids required in finished packaging).

home_compost.label: Limited or condition-specific evidence
home_compost.summary: Remains as mineral chalk/ash in the resulting compost. Harmless in modest amounts but does not bioconvert.
home_compost.limitations: Inert mineral residue; high concentrations leave chalky residues.

soil.label: Limited or condition-specific evidence
soil.summary: Naturally occurring mineral in limestone soils; dissolves slowly according to soil acidity (CaCO3 + 2H+ -> Ca2+ + H2O + CO2). Beneficial for liming acidic soils, but does not represent bioplastic polymer assimilation.
soil.limitations: Alters local soil pH if added in heavy concentrations.

freshwater.label: Limited or condition-specific evidence
freshwater.summary: Inorganic mineral; contributes to water hardness and alkalinity. Does not biodegrade enzymatically.

marine.label: Limited or condition-specific evidence
marine.summary: Primary constituent of marine invertebrate shells and coral; dissolves below the carbonate compensation depth. Does not undergo organic biological decomposition.

materials.disintegration_vs_biodegradation_notes: Mineral particles release when the surrounding biopolymer matrix degrades, remaining as microscopic mineral particles. This is mineral dissolution/dispersion, not biodegradation.
materials.recyclability_notes: Increases density of recycled polyolefins (sinks in water separation tanks); acceptable in controlled filler masterbatches.
materials.ecotoxicity_notes: Benign mineral salt. Heavy metal contamination (lead, cadmium, arsenic) from unrefined quarry sources must be independently tested against standard thresholds.

materials.name: Talc Mineral Filler

general_characteristics.typical_applications: Nucleating agent and stiffness enhancer in PLA thermoformed cutlery and packaging

industrial_compost.label: Limited or condition-specific evidence
industrial_compost.summary: Inorganic silicate mineral that does not biodegrade. Remains as inert mineral ash in finished compost. Must comply with EN 13432 ash content thresholds.
industrial_compost.limitations: Inorganic residue; excessive loading reduces volatile organic fraction required by composting specifications.

soil.label: Limited or condition-specific evidence
soil.summary: Insoluble phyllosilicate mineral; persists in soil as clay-like particulate without biological degradation.

freshwater.label: Limited or condition-specific evidence
freshwater.summary: Insoluble mineral particulate; settles into aquatic sediments.

marine.label: Limited or condition-specific evidence
marine.summary: Insoluble silicate mineral; deposits in sediment.

materials.disintegration_vs_biodegradation_notes: Inorganic minerals do not possess carbon-carbon bonds and cannot undergo microbial mineralization to carbon dioxide.
materials.recyclability_notes: Alters melt rheology and raises density in mechanical recycling.
materials.ecotoxicity_notes: Must be certified asbestos-free. Non-toxic silicate when free from respirable fibers and heavy metals.

materials.name: Acetyl Tributyl Citrate (ATBC Plasticizer)
materials.biobased_feedstock: Synthesized from naturally derived citric acid and butanol

general_characteristics.typical_applications: Non-toxic biodegradable plasticizer for PLA, PHB, and cellulose plastics

industrial_compost.label: Evidence supports biodegradation under the specified conditions
industrial_compost.summary: Readily accessible organic ester bonds are hydrolyzed and metabolized by composting microorganisms within 28-60 days.
industrial_compost.limitations: Plasticizer migration into packaged goods if improperly compounded.

home_compost.label: Evidence supports biodegradation under the specified conditions
home_compost.summary: Classified as inherently and readily biodegradable in mesophilic aerobic testing; degrades in ambient compost.

soil.label: Evidence supports biodegradation under the specified conditions
soil.summary: Soil bacteria metabolize citrate esters rapidly without accumulating toxic metabolites.
soil.limitations: None identified at standard formulation loadings (<10%).

freshwater.label: Evidence supports biodegradation under the specified conditions
freshwater.summary: Meets OECD 301 ready biodegradability criteria (>60% degradation in 28 days in aqueous medium).

marine.label: Limited or condition-specific evidence
marine.summary: Organic ester susceptible to marine esterases, but specific marine standard data are limited compared to freshwater tests.
references: Literature on aliphatic esters in marine systems
marine.limitations: Lack of standardized marine trial reports for neat additive.

materials.disintegration_vs_biodegradation_notes: Small organic molecule that dissolves and undergoes direct enzymatic beta-oxidation / Krebs cycle assimilation.
materials.recyclability_notes: Volatilizes or migrates during high-temperature recycling; lowers glass transition temperature of re-extruded blends.
materials.ecotoxicity_notes: Approved for food contact and pharmaceutical applications (FDA 21 CFR 175.105); negative for aquatic ecotoxicity in standard daphnia and fish assays.

materials.name: Titanium Dioxide (TiO2 White Pigment)

general_characteristics.typical_applications: White opacifying pigment and UV blocker in bioplastic and conventional packaging

industrial_compost.label: Limited or condition-specific evidence
industrial_compost.summary: Inorganic pigment; cannot biodegrade. Remains as persistent mineral pigment in the compost. Concentration must be kept below certification thresholds (<1-2%).
industrial_compost.limitations: Non-biodegradable mineral. Must not exceed standard chemical restriction limits.

home_compost.label: Limited or condition-specific evidence
home_compost.summary: Completely inert pigment; does not degrade.

soil.label: Limited or condition-specific evidence
soil.summary: Insoluble mineral pigment. If used in nanoscale form, poses documented risks of bioaccumulation and ecotoxicity to soil bacteria and earthworms.
soil.limitations: Nanoparticle variants raise significant terrestrial ecotoxicity concerns.

freshwater.label: Limited or condition-specific evidence
freshwater.summary: Insoluble particles settle in sediment. Nanoscale TiO2 induces photocatalytic reactive oxygen species (ROS) that harm aquatic micro-invertebrates.

marine.label: Limited or condition-specific evidence
marine.summary: Insoluble particulate; precipitates into marine sediments without organic degradation.

materials.disintegration_vs_biodegradation_notes: Inorganic pigment that never undergoes carbon mineralization; persists as microscopic or nanoscale particles.
materials.recyclability_notes: Pigment causes discoloration in natural/transparent recycling streams, downgrading recyclate to dark or opaque fractions.
materials.ecotoxicity_notes: EU banned TiO2 as a food additive (E171) in 2022 due to genotoxicity concerns of the nanoparticle fraction. Compost certification restricts nanoscale pigment additions.

materials.name: Carbon Black (Black Pigment)
materials.biobased_feedstock: Incomplete combustion of heavy petroleum fractions or vegetable oils

general_characteristics.typical_applications: Black masterbatch pigment in agricultural mulch films, trash bags, and electronic housings

industrial_compost.label: Limited or condition-specific evidence
industrial_compost.summary: Elemental carbon particles with turbostratic structure; virtually inert to microbial metabolism under composting durations. Allowed only under strict concentration caps (<1-2%) under EN 13432.
industrial_compost.limitations: Does not mineralize to CO2 within standard testing timeframes.

home_compost.label: Limited or condition-specific evidence
home_compost.summary: Inert elemental carbon; remains in the finished compost.

soil.label: Limited or condition-specific evidence
soil.summary: Behaves like ancient elemental black carbon / charcoal; high environmental persistence (>decades to centuries).
soil.limitations: Non-biodegradable; may carry polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbon (PAH) residues if unrefined.

freshwater.label: Limited or condition-specific evidence
freshwater.summary: Insoluble carbon particulate that settles in sediments.

marine.label: Limited or condition-specific evidence
marine.summary: Insoluble particle that deposits into marine sediments.

materials.disintegration_vs_biodegradation_notes: Elemental carbon particles do not evolve biogenic CO2 during respirometric tests; they are chemically inert particles.
materials.recyclability_notes: Severe issue in automated near-infrared (NIR) sorting systems at recycling facilities; traditional carbon black absorbs NIR radiation, making the sorting machine blind to the host polymer.
materials.ecotoxicity_notes: Must be tested for Polycyclic Aromatic Hydrocarbons (PAHs) to avoid heavy contamination in organic agriculture.

materials.name: Unknown Trade-Name Additive / Proprietary Masterbatch

general_characteristics.typical_applications: Processing lubricants, slip agents, compatibilizers, fragrance, anti-blocking

industrial_compost.label: Insufficient evidence
industrial_compost.summary: Chemical composition, molecular weight, and biodegradation kinetics are undisclosed. Scientific screening cannot assume biodegradability or compostability without full CAS disclosure or third-party test reports.
industrial_compost.limitations: Severe documentation gap. If additive exceeds 1% of formulation, EN 13432 / ASTM D6400 certification is invalid without individual testing.

home_compost.label: Insufficient evidence
home_compost.summary: No verified test reports or chemical composition available.
home_compost.limitations: Potential microplastic or toxic residue hazard.

soil.summary: Unknown persistence, biodegradation pathway, and soil ecotoxicity.

marine.summary: Undocumented marine persistence and biofilm interaction.

materials.disintegration_vs_biodegradation_notes: Undisclosed chemistry may contain non-biodegradable synthetic polymers (e.g. polyolefin waxes, fluorinated PFAS processing aids) that disintegrate into persistent micro-contaminants.
materials.recyclability_notes: Unknown compatibilizers can compromise both mechanical recycling and organic composting streams.
materials.ecotoxicity_notes: CRITICAL RISK: Without Safety Data Sheet (SDS) Section 3 disclosure and REACH / TSCA registration, ecotoxicity, plant inhibition, and PFAS content cannot be verified.
